title: Unit finite comparison formula
statement:
theorem finite_formula_unit_exists
    (b : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ leftComplex l E L ι g ≅
      (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ rightComplex l E L ι g)
    (hb : CompletedFormula l E L ι g b) :
    ∃ bfin : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ finiteLeft l E L ι g n ≅
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ finiteRight l E L ι g n,
      FiniteFormulaUnit l E L ι g bfin

proof.text: Identify unrestrictedIntegralReductionFunctor, finiteExtension, and integralScalarReduction with the existing sheafified extensionFunctor using their prescribed object and map equalities. The comparison components are eqToIso of the object equalities; inverse transports in the definitions of the pure tensors cancel these components.

Naturality of the normalized finite constant coefficient maps gives the square for the finite E-to-L scalar map. Cancel the two invertible coefficient maps to obtain the inverse-action square. This square defines an identity-on-underlying-sections isomorphism between the two composites of scalar restriction and inverse image.

Use the normalized adjunction transport construction of the quotient-chain calculation on this restriction square. Both sectionwise module inverse-image functors are equivalences, so its mate is invertible. The normalized adjunction unit shows that its pure-tensor rule transports the outer scalar through the inverse L coefficient map.

Compose finite scalar transport with the canonical scalar-extension reassociation for the completed E projection followed by the finite E-to-L map, and conjugate by the presentation isomorphisms from Step 1. On a double pure tensor the result is the inverse-transported outer scalar multiplied by the image of the middle scalar. Lift this natural module isomorphism termwise to cochain complexes, restrict to good complexes, and specialize the middle scalar to 1. This construction does not require the supplied completed comparison or its normalization.
